## Natural history notes

A microscopic freshwater euglenoid characterized by a long, rigid, spindle-shaped green cell that narrows into an elongated anterior “snout” and a sharply pointed tail. Lepocinclis acus contains numerous chloroplasts and conspicuous rod-shaped paramylon bodies used for carbohydrate storage, while fine spiral striations may be visible along the cell surface. It occurs as a free-swimming photosynthetic microorganism in freshwater habitats such as ponds, lakes, wetlands, and other standing or slow-moving waters. Formerly known as Euglena acus, it contributes to primary production and forms part of the planktonic microbial food web.
